:::{#exr-rss-hessian}
#### Second derivatives of RSS

Find the matrix of second derivatives of
$\text{RSS}(\intcoef, \coef{x})$ (@exm-rss-slr)
with respect to $\intcoef$ and $\coef{x}$,
and show that it is positive definite when $S_{xx} > 0$ (@def-centered-sums).
:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#sol-rss-hessian}

Differentiate each first derivative again.

**Derivatives of $\partial \text{RSS} / \partial \intcoef$.**
By @exr-rss-deriv-intercept,
$\partial \text{RSS} / \partial \intcoef
= -2 \paren{n \bar{y} - n \intcoef - \coef{x} n \bar{x}}$.
Differentiating with respect to $\intcoef$:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\frac{\partial^2 \text{RSS}}{\partial \intcoef^2}
&= -2 \deriv{\intcoef}
  \paren{n \bar{y} - n \intcoef - \coef{x} n \bar{x}}
&& \text{(constant factor)}\\
&= -2 \paren{
  \frac{\partial (n \bar{y})}{\partial \intcoef}
  - \frac{\partial (n \intcoef)}{\partial \intcoef}
  - \frac{\partial (\coef{x} n \bar{x})}{\partial \intcoef}}
&& \text{(derivative of a sum)}\\
&= -2 (0 - n - 0)
&& \text{(differentiate each term)}\\
&= -2 (-n)
&& \text{(drop the zeros)}\\
&= 2n
&& \text{(multiply)}
\end{aligned}
$$

Differentiating with respect to $\coef{x}$:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\frac{\partial^2 \text{RSS}}{\partial \coef{x} \, \partial \intcoef}
&= -2 \frac{\partial}{\partial \coef{x}}
  \paren{n \bar{y} - n \intcoef - \coef{x} n \bar{x}}
&& \text{(constant factor)}\\
&= -2 \paren{
  \frac{\partial (n \bar{y})}{\partial \coef{x}}
  - \frac{\partial (n \intcoef)}{\partial \coef{x}}
  - \frac{\partial (\coef{x} n \bar{x})}{\partial \coef{x}}}
&& \text{(derivative of a sum)}\\
&= -2 (0 - 0 - n \bar{x})
&& \text{(differentiate each term)}\\
&= -2 (-n \bar{x})
&& \text{(drop the zeros)}\\
&= 2 n \bar{x}
&& \text{(multiply)}
\end{aligned}
$$

{{< slidebreak >}}

**Derivatives of $\partial \text{RSS} / \partial \coef{x}$.**
By @exr-rss-deriv-slope,
$\partial \text{RSS} / \partial \coef{x}
= -2 \sumin x_i (y_i - \intcoef - \coef{x} x_i)$.
Differentiating with respect to $\intcoef$,
and reusing the inner derivative $-1$ from @exr-rss-deriv-intercept:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\frac{\partial^2 \text{RSS}}{\partial \intcoef \, \partial \coef{x}}
&= -2 \deriv{\intcoef} \sumin x_i (y_i - \intcoef - \coef{x} x_i)
&& \text{(constant factor)}\\
&= -2 \sumin \deriv{\intcoef} \paren{x_i (y_i - \intcoef - \coef{x} x_i)}
&& \text{(derivative of a sum)}\\
&= -2 \sumin x_i \deriv{\intcoef} (y_i - \intcoef - \coef{x} x_i)
&& \text{($x_i$ does not depend on $\intcoef$)}\\
&= -2 \sumin x_i (-1)
&& \text{(inner derivative is $-1$)}\\
&= -2 \sumin (-x_i)
&& \text{(multiply)}\\
&= -2 \paren{-\sumin x_i}
&& \text{(constant factor out of the sum)}\\
&= 2 \sumin x_i
&& \text{(multiply)}\\
&= 2 n \bar{x}
&& \text{($\sumin x_i = n \bar{x}$)}
\end{aligned}
$$

Differentiating with respect to $\coef{x}$,
and reusing the inner derivative $-x_i$ from @exr-rss-deriv-slope:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\frac{\partial^2 \text{RSS}}{\partial \coef{x}^2}
&= -2 \frac{\partial}{\partial \coef{x}} \sumin x_i (y_i - \intcoef - \coef{x} x_i)
&& \text{(constant factor)}\\
&= -2 \sumin \frac{\partial}{\partial \coef{x}} \paren{x_i (y_i - \intcoef - \coef{x} x_i)}
&& \text{(derivative of a sum)}\\
&= -2 \sumin x_i \frac{\partial}{\partial \coef{x}} (y_i - \intcoef - \coef{x} x_i)
&& \text{($x_i$ does not depend on $\coef{x}$)}\\
&= -2 \sumin x_i (-x_i)
&& \text{(inner derivative is $-x_i$)}\\
&= -2 \sumin \paren{-x_i^2}
&& \text{(multiply)}\\
&= -2 \paren{-\sumin x_i^2}
&& \text{(constant factor out of the sum)}\\
&= 2 \sumin x_i^2
&& \text{(multiply)}
\end{aligned}
$$

{{< slidebreak >}}

**The matrix.**
Collecting the four second derivatives,
the matrix of second derivatives is

$$
\begin{pmatrix} 2n & 2 n \bar{x} \\ 2 n \bar{x} & 2 \sumin x_i^2 \end{pmatrix}.
$$

Its top-left entry, $2n$, is positive.
Its determinant,
using the expanded form of $S_{xx}$ from @exr-sxx-expand, is

$$
\begin{aligned}
\det \begin{pmatrix} 2n & 2 n \bar{x} \\ 2 n \bar{x} & 2 \sumin x_i^2 \end{pmatrix}
&= (2n) \paren{2 \sumin x_i^2} - (2 n \bar{x}) (2 n \bar{x})
&& \text{($2 \times 2$ determinant)}\\
&= 4 n \sumin x_i^2 - 4 n^2 \bar{x}^2
&& \text{(multiply)}\\
&= 4 n \paren{\sumin x_i^2 - n \bar{x}^2}
&& \text{(factor out $4n$)}\\
&= 4 n S_{xx}
&& \text{(expanded form of $S_{xx}$)}
\end{aligned}
$$

which is positive when $S_{xx} > 0$.
A symmetric $2 \times 2$ matrix with a positive top-left entry
and a positive determinant is positive definite.

:::
